(4.57i)

5
Ward-Takahashi Identities for Braided Gauge Symmetries

In
section

4.2
we showed that the one-loop photon vacuum polarisation tensor
\Pi_{\star}(p)^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}
of braided scalar quantum electrodynamics is transverse:
p_{\mu}\,{\Pi}_{\star}^{\mu\nu}(p)^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}=0
. This reflects the Ward-Takahashi identity for the braided
\mathsf{U}(1)
gauge symmetry at the level of the vacuum polarisations. In this final section we use the braided
L_{\infty}
-structure and the homological perturbation lemma to extend this Ward-Takahashi identity to all loop orders for correlators involving the electric current.

Our homotopy algebraic formulation of the Ward-Takahashi identities is similar in spirit to other approaches which have appeared recently in the literature.
Linearised Ward identities for tree-level scattering amplitudes in Yang-Mills theory are established in
[
39
]
within the
L_{\infty}
-algebra framework. Scattering amplitudes are well understood in terms of a quasi-isomorphism onto the minimal model of the corresponding
L_{\infty}
-algebra
\mathscr{L}
, which in particular contains the asymptotically free fields (see e.g.
[
40
,
41
,
42
,
31
,
37
]
). When one of the fields in a scattering amplitude is taken to be trivial in the cohomology
H^{1}(L)
, then the amplitude vanishes as a direct consequence of the homotopy Jacobi identities in the minimal model
[
39
]
. The physical interpretation is that longitudinal external states do not contribute to the S-matrix.

Anomalous Ward-Takahashi identities for correlation functions involving Noether currents for general global symmetries of field theories are derived in
[
43
]
within the framework of quantum
A_{\infty}
-algebras. The derivation follows from an equivalent form of the homotopy algebraic Schwinger-Dyson equations from
[
34
,
44
,
45
]
, which are based on the homological perturbation lemma. The anomaly matches with known anomalies in examples.

We stress that our approach is fundamentally different: it is based on the underlying local BRST cohomology within our braided BV formalism. Combined with the braided homological perturbation lemma, this leads to a ‘master identity’ (see (
5.25
)) which is functionally similar to the algebraic Schwinger-Dyson equation of
[
43
, eq. (3.45)]
. Our Ward-Takahashi identity (see (
5.40
)) is then analogous to that of
[
43
, eq. (4.45)]
. However, in contrast to
[
43
]
, our derivation leads to an interpretation of the anomaly in terms of the BV Laplacian of the extended BRST functional for the matter fields.

5.1
Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin Transformations

In the BV formalism, the braided gauge symmetries of the classical Maurer-Cartan theory from
section

2.3
are promoted to nilpotent global symmetries of the extended BV theory from
section

3.1
.
Braided gauge transformations come from the BRST part
of the extended BV functional (
3.3
), evaluated in (
3.17
) for the quadratic vertex and in (
3.20
) for the cubic vertex.
This induces the nilpotent braided derivation of degree 1 given by

Q_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}:=\big\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(2)}}+\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,,\,-\big\}_{\star}:\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]\longrightarrow(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2])[1]\ ,

(5.1)

which is in fact a
strict
derivation by momentum conservation.

Acting on a basis of antifields for
L[2]^{0}
in momentum space, the BRST differential (
5.1
) describes the braided gauge transformations (
2.29
):

Q_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}\begin{pmatrix}\mathtt{e}^{p}\\[3.00003pt]
\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p}\\[3.00003pt]
\mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\displaystyle-\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}-p)\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{1}\cdot\theta\,k_{2}}\ \mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\widetilde{\texttt{e}}^{k_{2}}\\[13.00005pt]
\displaystyle\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}-p)\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{1}\cdot\theta\,k_{2}}\ \bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\widetilde{\texttt{e}}^{k_{2}}\\[13.00005pt]
\tfrac{\mathrm{i}}{g}\,p_{\mu}\ \mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{p}\end{pmatrix}\ ,

(5.2)

as expected from the
L_{\infty}
-structure of
section

2.3
.
A short calculation verifies
(Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}})^{2}=0
.

The classical extended action functional
\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}:=\mathcal{S}_{0}+\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{int}}\in(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2])^{0}
is invariant under BRST transformations if

Q_{{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\rm cl}=0\ ,

(5.3)

that is, it is braided gauge invariant. We verify (
5.3
) explicitly, using the vertices of the action functional from (
3.9
) and (
3.15
), along with the BRST transformations (
5.2
).

Recall that the free part of the action functional (
3.3
) is given by

\begin{split}\mathcal{S}_{0}=\frac{1}{2}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2})\,&\bigg(\big(k_{1}^{2}-m^{2}\big)\ \bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}+\big(k_{1}^{2}-m^{2}\big)\ \mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{2}}\\
&\qquad+\big(-k_{1}^{2}\,\eta^{\mu\nu}+k_{1}^{\mu}\,k_{1}^{\nu}\big)\ \mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\bigg)\ .\end{split}

(5.4a)

Applying the BRST transformations, we find

\begin{split}Q_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}\,\mathcal{S}_{0}&=\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\big(k_{2}^{2}-m^{2}\big)\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{2}\cdot\theta\,k_{3}}\\
&\hskip 199.16928pt\times\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\left(\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}-\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{3}}\right)\\[4.0pt]
&=\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\big(k_{2}^{2}-k_{3}^{2}\big)\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{2}\cdot\theta\,k_{3}}\ \mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}\ ,\end{split}

(5.4b)

where the contributions from the last entry of (
5.2
) vanish identically because of the projector
k^{2}\,\tilde{\mathsf{\Pi}}^{\mu\nu}(k)=k^{2}\,\eta^{\mu\nu}-k^{\mu}\,k^{\nu}
onto transverse momentum.

The cubic variation splits into an order
g^{0}
piece, in symmetric degree 3, and an order
g^{1}
piece, in symmetric degree 4.
One finds the non-vanishing BRST transformation

\begin{split}Q_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}\,\mathcal{S}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\mathrm{int}}&=-\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\big(k_{2}^{2}-k_{3}^{2}\big)\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{2}\cdot\theta\,k_{3}}\ \mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}\\
&\quad\,-\mathrm{i}\,g\,\int_{q_{1},q_{2}}\ \int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{8}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,(k_{2}-k_{3})^{\mu}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{2}\cdot\theta\,k_{3}+\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,q_{1}\cdot\theta\,q_{2}}\ \mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\\
&\hskip 142.26378pt\odot_{\star}\left(\delta(q_{1}+q_{2}-k_{2})\ \mathtt{e}^{q_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{q_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}\right.\\
&\hskip 199.16928pt\left.-\,\delta(q_{1}+q_{2}-k_{3})\ \mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{q_{1}}\odot_{\star}{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}}^{q_{2}}\right)\ .\end{split}

(5.4c)

The variation of the quartic part of the action functional is found to be

\begin{split}Q_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}\,\mathcal{S}^{\textrm{\tiny(4)}}_{\mathrm{int}}&=\mathrm{i}\,g\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3},k_{4}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3}+k_{4})\\
&\hskip 142.26378pt\times\left(k_{1}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{4}}\right.\\
&\hskip 199.16928pt\left.+\,\mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{k_{2}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{k_{3}}\odot_{\star}k_{4}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{4}}\right)\ .\end{split}

(5.4d)

The term of symmetric degree 5 contained in
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,\mathcal{S}^{\textrm{\tiny(4)}}_{\mathrm{int}}
, of order
g^{2}
, vanishes after a simple relabelling of momenta.

Summing the contributions in (
5.4
), we verify
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\rm cl}=0
.

5.2
Extended Electric Current

Braided gauge invariance of the Maurer-Cartan functional (
2.39
) is equivalent to the weak conservation of the braided electric current (
2.38
). We show that one can associate to the braided gauge invariant extended action functional
\mathcal{S}_{\rm cl}
a symmetrised current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}\in(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[1]^{*})^{0}
, whose correlators are also conserved.
The extended electric current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}
is the lift of the original braided Noether current
J^{\star}\in\Omega^{1}(\mathbbm{R}^{1,3})
to the symmetric algebra
\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[1]^{*}
.
Like the interaction terms of the extended BV functional, its form is much simpler than that of the original description, due to the braided symmetrisation.

The symmetric current

\displaystyle\mathcal{J}^{\star}=\mathcal{J}_{2}^{\star}+\mathcal{J}^{\star}_{3}\ \in\ (\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2])^{0}

(5.5)

is given in momentum space by the sum of the two contributions

\displaystyle\mathcal{J}_{2}^{\star\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})

\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\ \left(p_{1}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}-{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}p_{2}^{\mu}\,\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}\right)\ ,

(5.6)

\displaystyle\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(p_{1},p_{2},p_{3})

\displaystyle=-2\,g\,\eta^{\mu\nu}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,\sum\limits_{i<j}\,p_{i}\cdot\theta\,p_{j}}\ \mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{3}}\ .

(5.7)

We shall demonstrate that the extended current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}
is dual to the classical braided Noether current
J^{\star}\in\Omega^{1}(\mathbbm{R}^{1,3})
, written in its non-covariant form (
2.37
).

For this, we must first introduce a pairing between the respective symmetric algebras.
We define the pairing between braided symmetric elements of degree
n

\begin{split}\langle-,-\rangle_{\star}:\big(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}(L[1])^{*}\big)^{n}\otimes\big(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[1]\big)^{n}\longrightarrow\mathbbm{R}\end{split}

(5.8)

as

\begin{split}\langle\xi^{1}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\xi^{n}\,,\,\tau_{1}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\tau_{n}\rangle_{\star}:=\sum_{\sigma\in S_{n}}\,\pm\,\langle\xi^{1},\tau_{\sigma_{\mathcal{R}}(n)}\rangle_{\star}\cdots\langle\xi^{n},\tau_{{\sigma_{\mathcal{R}}(1)}}\rangle_{\star}\ ,\end{split}

(5.9)

for elements
\xi^{i}\in L[1]^{*}
and
\tau_{i}\in L[1]
, with
i=1,\dots,n
. Here
S_{n}
is the symmetric group of degree
n
, and the permutation
\sigma_{\mathcal{R}}
acts by braided graded transposition.
For example, on quadratic symmetric powers the pairing is

\begin{split}\langle\xi^{1}\odot_{\star}\xi^{2}\,,\,\tau_{1}\odot_{\star}\tau_{2}\rangle_{\star}&=\langle\xi^{1},\tau_{2}\rangle_{\star}\;\langle\xi^{2},\tau_{1}\rangle_{\star}\pm\langle\xi^{1},\mathsf{R}_{\alpha}(\tau_{1})\rangle_{\star}\;\langle\mathsf{R}^{\alpha}(\xi^{2}),\tau_{2}\rangle_{\star}\ .\end{split}\,

(5.10)

Consider the superfield
\mathcal{A}\in L^{1}
of (
2.6
).
By shifting the degree using the suspension isomorphism
s:L\longrightarrow L[1]
, this defines a degree 0 element which has momentum space decomposition given by

s\mathcal{A}=\begin{pmatrix}\displaystyle\int_{k}\,\widehat{\phi}(k)\ \mathtt{e}_{k}\\[13.00005pt]
\displaystyle\int_{k}\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(k)\ \bar{\mathtt{e}}_{k}\\[13.00005pt]
\ \displaystyle\int_{k}\,\widehat{A}{}_{\mu}(k)\ \mathtt{v}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}_{k}\end{pmatrix}\ \in\ L[1]^{0}\ .

(5.11)

The degree is carried by basis elements
\mathtt{e}_{k}
,
\mathtt{\bar{e}}_{k}
and
\mathtt{v}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}_{k}
of degree 0, which are dual to their respective antifield bases as explained in
section

2.4
.

Then the pairing of a quadratic basis antifield
\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}
with symmetrised superfields is

\begin{split}\langle\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}\,,\,\tfrac{1}{2}\,s\mathcal{A}\odot_{\star}s\mathcal{A}\rangle_{\star}&=\frac{1}{2}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,\Big(\langle\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}},{\mathtt{e}}_{k_{2}}\rangle_{\star}\,\widehat{\phi}(k_{2})\ \langle\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}},\bar{\mathtt{e}}_{k_{1}}\rangle_{\star}\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(k_{1})\\
&\hskip 71.13188pt+\langle\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}},\mathsf{R}_{\alpha}({\mathtt{e}}_{k_{1}})\rangle_{\star}\,\widehat{\phi}(k_{1})\ \langle\mathsf{R}^{\alpha}(\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}),\bar{\mathtt{e}}_{k_{2}}\rangle_{\star}\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(k_{2})\Big)\ .\end{split}

(5.12)

Using the dual pairings
\langle\mathtt{e}^{p},\mathtt{e}_{k}\rangle_{\star}=(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p-k)=\langle\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p},\bar{\mathtt{e}}_{k}\rangle_{\star}
, and multiplying with the phase factor entering the quadratic part of the extended current (
5.6
), we find

\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\langle\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}\,,\,\tfrac{1}{2}\,s\mathcal{A}\odot_{\star}s\mathcal{A}\rangle_{\star}=\tfrac{1}{2}\,\big(\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\widehat{\phi}(p_{1})\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(p_{2})+\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\widehat{\phi}(p_{1})\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(p_{2})\big)\ ,

(5.13)

which we recognise as the momentum space coordinate function of
\frac{1}{2}\,(\phi\star\bar{\phi}+\bar{\phi}\star\phi)
.
Multiplying by the appropriate momenta, we recover the quadratic part of (
2.37
).

Similarly, with the dual pairing on photon states
\langle\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\texttt{e}^{k},\mathtt{v}^{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}_{p}\rangle_{\star}=(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta_{\mu}^{\nu}\,\delta(k-p)
we find that the pairing with symmetric degree 3 symmetrised superfields of the cubic extended current (
5.7
) is

\begin{split}&\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,\sum\limits_{i<j}\,p_{i}\cdot\theta\,p_{j}}\,\langle\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\bar{\mathtt{e}}^{p_{2}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\mu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{3}}\,,\,\tfrac{1}{6}\,s\mathcal{A}\odot_{\star}s\mathcal{A}\odot_{\star}s\mathcal{A}\rangle_{\star}\\[4.0pt]
&\hskip 170.71652pt=\frac{1}{6}\,\sum_{\sigma\in S_{3}}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,\sum\limits_{i<j}\,p_{\sigma(i)}\cdot\theta\,p_{\sigma(j)}}\,\widehat{\phi}(p_{1})\,\widehat{\bar{\phi}}(p_{2})\,\widehat{A}_{\mu}(p_{3})\ .\end{split}

(5.14)

We recognise this as the momentum space coordinate function of the cubic part of (
2.37
).

Therefore the extended electric current is related to the classical Noether current if we pair each term
\mathcal{J}_{2}^{\star}
and
\mathcal{J}_{3}^{\star}
with the appropriate symmetric power of the superfield
s\mathcal{A}
.
If we introduce a symmetric exponential from the superfield
s\mathcal{A}\in L[1]^{0}
as

\mathrm{e}^{s\mathcal{A}}_{0}:=\sum_{n\geq 1}\,\frac{1}{n!}\,(s\mathcal{A})^{\odot_{\star}n}\ ,

(5.15)

understood as living in a suitable completion of
(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[1])^{0}
, then the classical Noether current is recovered by composing the pairing with the projection onto the subspace
\mathbbm{R}
.
We denote this projection by
\mathrm{pr}_{\mathbbm{R}}
, which restricts the pairing between components of like degrees. Then

\mathrm{pr}_{\mathbbm{R}}\,\langle\mathcal{J}^{\star},\mathrm{e}_{0}^{s\mathcal{A}}\rangle_{\star}=J^{\star}\ ,

(5.16)

where
J^{\star}
is the braided Noether current (
2.38
).

This shows that the extended current is the lift to the symmetric algebra of the classical electric current.
The braided gauge invariance of the weakly conserved current (
2.38
) is also lifted to the invariance of the conserved current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}
in the symmetric algebra, which can be expressed simply as

Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}=0\ .

(5.17)

Similarly to the classical Noether current, the braided extended current appears in the BRST transformation of the scalar fields alone, which is generated by the operator
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}:=\{\mathcal{S}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}},-\}_{\star}
.
Indeed, by isolating such contributions from (
5.4
) we find

\begin{split}Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\rm cl}&=\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{1\,\mu})\ \mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{J}_{2}^{\star}{}^{\mu}(k_{2},k_{3})\\
&\quad\,+\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3},k_{4}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3}+k_{4})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{1\,\mu})\ \mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{J}_{3}^{\star}{}^{\mu}(k_{2},k_{3},k_{4})\ .\end{split}

(5.18)

The remaining BRST transformation of the photon field is generated by the operator
\{\mathcal{S}^{\textrm{\tiny(2)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}},-\}_{\star}
. The decomposition of (
5.3
) in this way is the extended version of the decomposition of the classical braided Noether identity (
2.36
), wherein we recognise the operator
-\mathrm{i}\,k_{1\,\mu}
as the codifferential
\mathrm{d}^{\dagger}
in momentum space after resolving the delta-distributions.

5.3
Anomalous Ward Identity

We show how the Ward identity is an immediate consequence of the homological perturbation lemma.

Master Identity.

Consider the strong deformation retract (
3.41
) defined by the small perturbation
\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
from (
3.36
), the classical free projection
\mathsf{P}_{0}
onto
\mathbbm{R}\simeq\big(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}H^{\bullet}(L[2])\big)^{0}
from (
3.26
), and the canonical inclusion
\mathsf{I}_{0}
of
\mathbbm{R}
into
\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]
. In the remainder of this section we make extensive use of the key identity

\displaystyle\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ(\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\star}_{1}+\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}})=0\ ,

(5.19)

where
\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}:=\mathsf{P}_{0}+\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
.

To prove (
5.19
), we use the homological perturbation lemma which asserts that the deformed projection
\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}
remains a cochain map:

\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ(\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\star}_{1}+\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}})=\boldsymbol{{\delta}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\ .

(5.20)

The homological perturbation lemma also provides explicit formulas for the maps

\boldsymbol{{\delta}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}=\mathsf{P}_{0}\,\big(\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]}-\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\,\mathsf{H}\big)^{-1}\,\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\,\mathsf{I}_{0}\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}=\mathsf{P}_{0}\,\big(\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]}-\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\,\mathsf{H}\big)^{-1}\ .

(5.21)

As
\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}
is based around the trivial projection
\mathsf{P}_{0}
to
\mathbbm{R}
, and since the perturbation
\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
acts trivially on the ground field
\mathbbm{R}\subset\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]
, i.e.
\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}(\mathbbm{1})=0
, it follows that the composition
\boldsymbol{{\delta}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}=0
, which implies (
5.19
).

Among other things, this identity encompasses the algebraic Schwinger-Dyson equations of
[
34
,
44
,
45
,
43
,
7
]
.
For this, we first notice that the homological perturbation lemma implies
\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\mathsf{H}=0
, since
\mathsf{P}_{0}\circ\mathsf{H}=0
and
\mathsf{H}^{2}=0
, whereas
\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\mathsf{I}_{0}=\mathsf{P}_{0}\circ\mathsf{I}_{0}=\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}H^{\bullet}(L[2])}
using
\mathsf{H}\circ\mathsf{I}_{0}=0
.
Consider the precomposition of (
5.19
) with the free contracting homotopy
\mathsf{H}
. This implies
\mathsf{{P}}_{{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}}^{\prime}\circ(\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\star}_{1}+\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}})\circ\mathsf{H}=0
, and therefore

\mathsf{{P}}_{{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}}^{\prime}\circ\boldsymbol{\ell}^{\star}_{1}\circ\mathsf{H}=-\mathsf{{P}}_{{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}}^{\prime}\circ\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\circ\mathsf{H}\ .

(5.22)

Using the homotopy equivalence equation (
3.24
) of the free theory this implies

\displaystyle\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\big(-\mathsf{H}\circ\boldsymbol{\ell}_{1}^{\star}-\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2]}+\mathsf{I}_{0}\circ\mathsf{P_{0}}\big)

\displaystyle=-\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\circ\mathsf{H}\ ,

(5.23)

and therefore

\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}=\mathsf{P}_{0}+\mathsf{{P}}_{{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}}^{\prime}\circ\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\circ\mathsf{H}\ .

(5.24)

We recognise (
5.24
) as the algebraic Schwinger-Dyson equation, as derived in
[
7
]
.

We study correlation functions by using this identity applied to insertions of fields in
L[2]^{-1}
.
Then by (
5.19
), we get the identity

\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ(\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},-\}_{\star}+\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}})=0\ .

(5.25)

With
\mathsf{P}_{0}
projecting all elements with non-zero symmetric degree to
0
, the correlation functions are unchanged if one considers
\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
as previously, or the full projection
\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}
.
In short, elements in the image of the quantum differential

Q_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}=\boldsymbol{\ell}_{1}^{\star}+\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}=\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},-\}_{\star}+\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}

(5.26)

have vanishing correlation functions coming from application of
\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
.

Consistency of Braided Gauge Symmetries.

Recall that a gauge symmetry in a conventional quantum field theory is non-anomalous if the correlation functions are all invariant under gauge transformations implemented by the conserved charge operator and the vacuum expectation values of the associated Noether current operator are conserved to all orders in perturbation theory. In braided scalar QED, the action of braided gauge symmetries does not follow the traditional properties
[
1
,
2
]
. Hence the requirement that it be anomaly-free is non-trivial and needs to be checked thoroughly.

In braided scalar QED, the current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}\in(\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2])^{0}
is non-anomalous if its correlators are coclosed off-shell, which translates to checking

\partial_{\mu}\,\Big(\,\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\,\mathsf{P}_{0}\,(\boldsymbol{\delta}_{\hbar,{\rm int}}\,\mathsf{H}\big)^{k}\,(\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu})\Big)=0\ ,

(5.27)

for the usual deformation retract (
3.41
). We verify this to all orders in homological perturbation theory.

For this, we apply the identity (
5.25
) to a functional of degree
-1
living in the image of the BRST operator.
To obtain the Ward identity, we consider the scalar field transformation generated by
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}
on ghost fields,

Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}=\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\ \in\ L[2]^{-1}\ ,

(5.28)

where
\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\in(L[2])^{-2}
is the momentum basis for the ghost fields.
Recall the duality between ghost field/antifield pairs in momentum space given by
\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{1}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k_{2}}\}_{\star}=(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}-k_{2})
, with dual basis
\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k}\in L[2]^{1}
.
Applying the identity (
5.25
) to
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}
yields

\begin{split}\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\circ(\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},-\}_{\star}+\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}})\circ\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}&=0\ .\end{split}

(5.29)

We use the braided Jacobi identity to get

\begin{split}\hskip-14.22636pt\big\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}\,,\,\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\big\}_{\star}&=-\big\{\mathsf{R}_{\alpha}(\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}})\,,\,\{\mathsf{R}^{\alpha}(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}),\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\big\}_{\star}\\
&\hskip 28.45274pt-\big\{\mathsf{R}_{\alpha}\,\mathsf{R}_{\beta}(\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k})\,,\,\{\mathsf{R}^{\alpha}(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}),\mathsf{R}^{\beta}(\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}})\}_{\star}\big\}_{\star}=-\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\ .\end{split}

(5.30)

For the first equality we used the fact that
\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}
and
\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}
have degree
0
, while
\widetilde{\texttt{e}}_{k}
has degree
-2
, so the grading factor is always 1 in the braided Jacobi identity of
[
5
]
.
In the second equality we used the fact that the actions of
R
-matrices on
\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}
and
\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}
trivialise by translation invariance, and that the classical action functional does not contain ghost antifields, so
\left\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\right\}_{\star}=0
and the first term vanishes.
Finally, the pairing with the classical action functional can be written as
\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\}_{\star}=\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}\}_{\star}=Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}
.

The BV Laplacian is a strict graded derivation of the antibracket, hence

\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}=\{\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}+\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\ \ .

(5.31)

The second term vanishes since
\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}=0
.

Putting everything together, we have derived the
anomalous
Ward identity

\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\,\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}=\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\,\{\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\ .

(5.32)

The first term is related to the codifferential of the extended electric current derived in (
5.18
) through the pairing with the ghost field
\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}
:

\begin{split}&\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}=\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\\[5.0pt]
&\hskip 113.81102pt+\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\ .\end{split}

(5.33)

The resulting identity links the off-shell conservation of a current to the BV Laplacian of the BRST functional.
Braided scalar QED is non-anomalous since
\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}=0
, which can be seen using the decomposition of the ghost three-point vertex derived in (
3.20
):
The contributions from the two vertices cancel each other out.
This result enforces the current conservation in momentum space representation

\begin{split}&\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\,\big(\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\big)\\
&\hskip 56.9055pt+\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\,\big(\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\big)=0\end{split}

(5.34)

at all orders of perturbation theory.
Thus the braided gauge symmetry is non-anomalous. The vanishing of the left-hand side of (
5.34
) is a trivial consequence of momentum conservation in correlation functions, which sets the total momentum of each current component to zero.

5.4
Anomalous Ward-Takahashi Identities

We extend the result of
section

5.3
to correlation functions of the extended electric current together with field insertions.
Let
\mathcal{O}\in(L[2]^{0})^{\odot_{\star}n}
be a symmetric polynomial of antifields only.
Then
\mathcal{O}
trivially satisfies
\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{O}=0
and
\left\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\,,\,\mathcal{O}\right\}_{\star}=0
for a ghost basis field
\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\in L[2]^{-2}
.
We also have
\left\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathcal{O}\right\}_{\star}=0
, since the classical action functional acts non-trivially only on fields in
L[2]^{-1}
and
\mathcal{O}
is an antifield.

We apply the identity (
5.25
) to functionals of the form

Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\,\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}=\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\ \in\ (\mathrm{Sym}_{\star}L[2])^{-1}\ .

(5.35)

We first need to evaluate the image of this term under the quantum differential, which is given by

\big(\left\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},-\right\}_{\star}+\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\big)\circ(Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\,\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O})\ .

(5.36)

We split the calculation into two terms.

The antibracket is a braided graded derivation over
\odot_{\star}
, where we use the grading factors of
[
5
]
with
\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}
,
\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}
and
\mathcal{O}
of degree
0
, while
Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}
has degree
-1
.
We consider the term

\begin{split}\hskip-28.45274pt\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}&=\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}-\mathsf{R}_{\alpha}(Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k})\odot_{\star}\big\{\mathsf{R}^{\alpha}(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}}),\mathcal{O}\big\}_{\star}\\[4.0pt]
&=-\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\ .\end{split}

(5.37)

In the second equality we used the fact that
\left\{\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},-\right\}_{\star}
acts trivially on braided symmetric tensor products of antifields, together with (
5.30
).

For the next term, we recall that the BV Laplacian is a strict graded derivation over
\odot_{\star}
up to an antibracket contribution.
We then have

\begin{split}\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\big(\big\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\big)&=\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}-\{\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{O}\\
&\hskip 56.9055pt+\big\{\{\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star},\mathcal{O}\big\}_{\star}\\[4.0pt]
&=\{\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}+\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}\ .\end{split}

(5.38)

In the second equality we used
\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{O}=0=\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}
.
The final term is evaluated using the compatibility of the BRST differential with the antibracket, which follows from the Jacobi identity:

\begin{split}Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}&=\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}+\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{O}\}\ .\end{split}

(5.39)

Since
\left\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathcal{O}\right\}_{\star}=0
, this implies
\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}=-\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}
.

Altogether, applying the identity (
5.25
) to functionals of the form (
5.35
) implies

\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\big)+\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}\big)=\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(\{\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\big)\ .

(5.40)

This is the anomalous Ward-Takahashi identity.
In the present case, the anomaly vanishes since
\mathsf{\Delta}_{\textrm{\tiny BV}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}=0
, and we obtain in momentum space

\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}\big)=-\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{{P}}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{O}\}_{\star}\big)\ ,

(5.41)

where the left-hand side is related to the extended electric current through (
5.33
). We consider various explicit examples below.

Improper Three-Vertex Function.

In textbook quantum field theory, an amputated correlator obtained by applying the Maxwell operator to an external on-shell photon leg of a correlation function using the LSZ reduction formula is called an
improper
vertex function
[
46
]
.
Our main example is the derivation of the braided Ward-Takahashi identity for the improper scalar-scalar-photon vertex, sometimes called the electromagnetic vertex.

Following
[
46
]
, a vertex amputated of a single on-shell photon leg may be calculated by replacing the Maxwell operator
(\eta^{\mu\nu}\,\square-\partial^{\mu}\,\partial^{\nu})\,A_{\nu}
in the LSZ formula with the associated Noether current
g\,J^{\mu}
inside the correlation function, since
\mathcal{F}^{\mu}_{A}=\square\,A^{\mu}-\partial^{\mu}\,\partial_{\nu}\,A^{\nu}-g\,J^{\mu}=0
is the equation of motion for an on-shell photon field
A\in L[2]^{-1}
in the unextended theory.
In our framework of braided homological perturbation theory, we lift the equation of motion
\mathcal{F}^{\star\mu}_{A}=\ell_{1}^{\star}(A)^{\mu}-g\,J^{\star\mu}=0
to the symmetric algebra using the procedure discussed in
section

5.2
. This shows how correlation functions containing the symmetric current
g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}
from (
5.6
) and (
5.7
) can be interpreted as improper vertices.

We now show that the identity (
5.41
) is exactly the relation required to derive the braided deformation of the commutative Ward identity for the electromagnetic vertex
[
46
]
.
Consider the insertion of the scalar pair
\mathcal{O}=\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}
in the braided Ward-Takahashi identity giving

\mathsf{{P}}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\big(\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\big)=-\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,\mathsf{{P}}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\,\big\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,(\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}})\big\}_{\star}\ .

(5.42)

Let us first study the left-hand side of (
5.42
).
Using (
5.33
), we simply append a pair of scalars to find

\begin{split}&\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\\[4.0pt]
&\hskip 28.45274pt=\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\\
&\hskip 56.9055pt+\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,(-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu})\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\ .\end{split}

(5.43)

We introduce the one-form
C^{\star}\in\Omega^{1}\big((\mathbbm{R}^{1,3})^{\times 3}\big)
with momentum space components

\begin{split}\hskip-2.84526ptC^{\star\mu}(k,p_{1},p_{2})&:=\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\big)\\
&\quad\ +\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.44)

whose codifferential
-\mathrm{i}\,k_{\mu}\,C^{\star\mu}(k,p_{1},p_{2})
is the projection under
\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
of the right-hand side of (
5.43
), times a factor of the electromagnetic coupling
g
.
The integrand is a sum of a four-point and a five-point correlation function, which due to momentum conservation imposed by the map
\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
comes with an overall delta-distribution
(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+p_{2}-k)
. Hence (
5.44
) can be viewed as a three-point diagram.

We now turn to the right-hand side of the Ward-Takahashi identity (
5.42
).
We first use the dual pairing between ghost field/antifields given by
\left\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{p}\right\}_{\star}=(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k-p)
, together with the matter BRST transformation from (
5.1
), to express

\begin{split}\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\}_{\star}&=-\mathrm{i}\,\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(k_{1}+k_{2}-p_{1})\,\mathtt{e}^{k_{1}}\,\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{k_{2}}\}_{\star}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\,k_{1}\cdot\theta\,k}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k_{1}\cdot\theta\,k_{2}}\\[4.0pt]
&=-\mathrm{i}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{1}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}-k}\ ,\end{split}

(5.45)

and similarly
\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}\}_{\star}=\mathrm{i}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}-k}
.
Since
\left\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\right\}_{\star}=0
, i.e. the ghost field acts trivially on antifields in
L[2]^{0}
, we get

\begin{split}\big\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,(\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}})\big\}_{\star}=\mathrm{i}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\mathrm{i}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{1}}\,\big(-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{1}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}-k}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}}+\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}-k}\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.46)

where an extra
R
-matrix appears when commuting
\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k}
with
\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}
.

It is now just a matter of taking the interacting projection
\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}
to find the right hand side of the Ward-Takahashi identity from

\begin{split}\mathsf{{P}}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\big(\{\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}_{k},Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}\,(\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{p_{2}})\}_{\star}\big)&=\mathrm{i}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\mathrm{i}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{1}}\,\big(\mathrm{e}^{\,\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1},p_{2}-k)\\
&\hskip 113.81102pt-\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,k\cdot\theta\,p_{1}}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1}-k,p_{2})\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.47)

where the full scalar propagator is defined as
\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1},p_{2}):=\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}(\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\widetilde{e}}^{p_{2}})
.
By combining (
5.44
) and (
5.47
) into the braided Ward-Takahashi identity (
5.42
) we find

\begin{split}&k_{\mu}\,C^{\star\mu}(k,p_{1},p_{2})=\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\big(\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1},p_{2}-k)-\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1}-k,p_{2})\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.48)

where we used momentum conservation. This is the braided deformation of the commutative Ward identity for the electromagnetic vertex, which we have obtained as a direct consequence of the homological perturbation lemma.

The identity (
5.48
) involves all diagrams. We can extract a simpler identity for the fully amputated exact three-point vertex function
\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})
, which involves only 1PI contributions and recovers the textbook-type analytical expression. This is
thought of as the one-form
C^{\star}
amputated of its two remaining external scalar legs which come from combining the explicit scalar antifields on the right-hand side of (
5.44
) with the scalar antifields in the current
\mathcal{J}^{\star}
to generate propagators. For this, we dress the full propagator
\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1},p_{2})
with the scalar self-energy
\Sigma_{\star}(p)
at all loops:

\mathsf{\tilde{G}}^{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}_{\phi,\bar{\phi}}(p_{1},p_{2}):=-\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+p_{2})\ \frac{1}{p_{1}^{2}-m^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{1})}\ ,

(5.49)

and write

\displaystyle C^{\star\mu}(k,p_{1},p_{2})=(-\mathrm{i}\,\hbar)^{2}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+p_{2}-k)\ \frac{\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})}{\big(p_{1}^{2}-m^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{1})\big)\,\big(p_{2}^{2}-m^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{2})\big)}\ .

(5.50)

Upon substitution into (
5.48
) we then find

\displaystyle(p_{1}+p_{2})_{\mu}\,\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})=g\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\big[\big(p_{1}^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{1})\big)-\big(p_{2}^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{2})\big)\big]\ .

(5.51)

The identity (
5.51
) involves only 1PI diagrams.
It relates the full amputated three-vertex function
\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})
to the full scalar propagator
\big(p^{2}-m^{2}-\Sigma_{\star}(p)\big)^{-1}
,
which in the commutative limit
\theta=0
matches Takahashi’s identity in ordinary scalar QED.

We can easily illustrate the identity (
5.51
) to leading orders in homological perturbation theory using the explicit results of
section

4.3
and
section

4.4
, understood formally throughout with reflection symmetric cutoff regularisation of all loop integrals.
At tree-level, from (
4.40
) we find

\displaystyle\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(0)}}=g\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,(p_{1}-p_{2})^{\mu}\ ,

(5.52)

whose codifferential is

\displaystyle(p_{1}+p_{2})_{\mu}\,\Gamma_{\star}^{\mu}(p_{1},p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(0)}}=g\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\big(p_{1}^{2}-p_{2}^{2}\big)\ .

(5.53)

Since
\Sigma_{\star}(p)^{\textrm{\tiny(0)}}=0
from (
4.26
), this is indeed (
5.51
) at tree-level.

At one-loop order, after simplifying the integrands in (
4.56
) using the transverse projector
\tilde{\mathsf{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)
we find

\begin{split}\Gamma^{\mu}_{\star}(p_{1},p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}&=-4\,\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g^{3}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\bigg(\int_{q}\,p_{1}^{\lambda}\,p_{2}^{\alpha}\,(-2q+p_{1}-p_{2})^{\mu}\,\\
&\hskip 184.9429pt\times\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q-p_{1})\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q+p_{2})\,\mathsf{\tilde{D}}(q)\,\mathsf{\tilde{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)\\
&\hskip 113.81102pt+\int_{q}\,\eta^{\lambda\mu}\,\left(p_{1}^{\alpha}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q+p_{1})\,\mathsf{\tilde{D}}(q)\,\mathsf{\tilde{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)\right.\\
&\hskip 184.9429pt\left.-\,p_{2}^{\alpha}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q+p_{2})\,\mathsf{\tilde{D}}(q)\,\mathsf{\tilde{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)\right)\bigg)\ .\end{split}

(5.54)

We contract this with the external momentum
(p_{1}+p_{2})_{\mu}
and use the identity

\displaystyle(p_{1}+p_{2})\cdot(-2q+p_{1}-p_{2})=\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(p_{1}-q)^{-1}-\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(p_{2}+q)^{-1}\ .

(5.55)

Using the reflection symmetry
q\longmapsto-q
of the integral, together with the fact that all propagators are even functions, we then find that the cross-terms proportional to
p_{1}^{\lambda}\,p_{2}^{\alpha}
and
p_{1}^{\alpha}\,p_{2}^{\lambda}
cancel between the two integrals.

The codifferential of the three-vertex at one-loop reduces to

\begin{split}(p_{1}+p_{2})_{\mu}\,\Gamma^{\mu}_{\star}(p_{1},p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}&=-4\,\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g^{3}\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\\
&\hskip 56.9055pt\times\int_{q}\,\left(p_{1}^{\lambda}\,p_{1}^{\alpha}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q+p_{1})\,-\,p_{2}^{\lambda}\,p_{2}^{\alpha}\,\mathsf{\tilde{G}}(q+p_{2})\right)\,\mathsf{\tilde{D}}(q)\,\mathsf{\tilde{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)\ .\end{split}

(5.56)

By rewriting the one-loop scalar self-energy from (
4.38
) as

\Sigma_{\star}(p)^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}=4\,\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g^{2}\,\int_{q}\,\,p^{\lambda}\,p^{\alpha}\,\tilde{\sf{G}}(q+p)\,\tilde{\sf D}(q)\,\tilde{\mathsf{\Pi}}_{\lambda\alpha}(q)+3\,\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g^{2}\,\int_{q}\,\mathsf{\tilde{D}}(q)\ ,

(5.57)

it follows that

(p_{1}+p_{2})_{\mu}\,\Gamma^{\mu}_{\star}(p_{1},p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}=-g\,\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\mathrm{i}}{2}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2}}\,\big(\Sigma_{\star}(p_{1})^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}-\Sigma_{\star}(p_{2})^{\textrm{\tiny(1)}}\big)\ .

(5.58)

This is indeed (
5.51
) at one-loop order.

Photon Propagator.

Consider now the Ward-Takahashi identity (
5.41
) for an insertion of a single photon antifield
\mathcal{O}=\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{2}}\in L[2]^{0}
.
Since the cubic part of the BRST operator acts trivially on photon antifields, this example yields the simple identity

\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\big(\{Q_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}\,\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{cl}},\mathtt{\tilde{e}}_{p_{1}}\}_{\star}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{2}}\big)=0\ .

(5.59)

Introducing the rank two tensor
D^{\star}
on
\mathbbm{R}^{1,3}\times\mathbbm{R}^{1,3}
with momentum space components

\begin{split}D^{\star\mu}_{\nu}(p_{1},p_{2})&:=\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+k_{1}+k_{2})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{2}}\big)\\
&\quad\ +\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\nu}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{2}}\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.60)

then (
5.59
) is written as

p_{1\,\mu}\,D^{\star\mu}_{\nu}(p_{1},p_{2})=0\ .

(5.61)

From (
5.6
) and (
5.7
) it follows that
D^{\star}
is of order
g^{2}
. By interpreting it as a two-point correlation function with one external photon leg amputated, we write

{D}^{\star\mu}_{\nu}(p_{1},p_{2}):=\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}-p_{2})\,\Pi_{\star}^{\mu\lambda}(p_{1})\,\bigg(\frac{1}{\eta-\tilde{\mathsf{D}}(p_{1})\,\tilde{\mathsf{\Pi}}(p_{1})\,\Pi_{\star}(p_{1})}\bigg)_{\lambda\rho}\,\tilde{\mathsf{D}}(p_{2})\,\tilde{\mathsf{\Pi}}^{\rho}_{\nu}(p_{2})\ ,

(5.62)

where
\Pi_{\star}(p)
is the photon vacuum polarisation tensor, which receives contributions from only 1PI diagrams and which we calculated at one-loop order in
section

4.2
.
Then the identity (
5.61
) implies that the photon vacuum polarisation is transverse at all loop orders:

p_{\mu}\,\Pi_{\star}^{\mu\nu}(p)=0\ .

(5.63)

In other words, the Ward identity holds for braided scalar QED at all loop orders.

More General Identities.

The calculations above can be readily extended to insertions of arbitrary numbers of conjugate pairs of scalar antifields as well as of photon antifields:

\displaystyle\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{(m,n)}:=\mathtt{v}_{\mu_{2}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{2}}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\mu_{m}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{m}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{q_{1}}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{q_{n}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{\bar{q}_{1}}\odot_{\star}\ldots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{\bar{q}_{n}}\ .

(5.64)

We use
Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}
acting as a strict derivation trivially on photon antifields, and resolving the
R
-matrices on
n
insertions of scalar antifields as well as on a product of conjugate scalar antifields.

Introduce the rank
m
tensor
D_{(m,n)}^{\star}
on
(\mathbbm{R}^{1,3})^{\times(m+2n)}
with components

\begin{split}&D^{\star\mu_{1}}_{(m,n)\mu_{2}\cdots\mu_{m}}(p_{1},\dots,p_{m};q_{1},\dots,q_{n};\bar{q}_{1},\dots,\bar{q}_{n})\\[4.0pt]
&\hskip 56.9055pt:=\int_{k_{1},k_{2}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+k_{1}+k_{2})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{2}(k_{1},k_{2})\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}_{(m,n}\big)\\
&\hskip 85.35826pt+\int_{k_{1},k_{2},k_{3}}\,(2\pi)^{4}\,\delta(p_{1}+k_{1}+k_{2}+k_{3})\,\mathsf{P}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}^{\prime}\big(g\,\mathcal{J}^{\star\mu}_{3}(k_{1},k_{2},k_{3})\odot_{\star}\mathcal{O}_{(m,n)}\big)\ ,\end{split}

(5.65)

with labels of incoming momenta
\{p_{i}\}_{i=1}^{m}
,
\{q_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}
and
\{\bar{q}_{i}\}_{i=1}^{n}
for photons, scalars and conjugate scalars respectively. Its codifferential
-\mathrm{i}\,p_{1\,\mu_{1}}\,D^{\star\mu_{1}}_{(m,n)\mu_{2}\cdots\mu_{m}}
is the left-hand side of the Ward-Takahashi identity times a factor of
g
. Below we will use the shorthand
p_{1\cdots k}=p_{1}+\cdots+p_{k}
for sums of momenta.

We obtain a relation between
D^{\star}_{(m,n)}
and a sum of exact correlation functions of lower order.
Denote the exact correlation function of
m
photons and
n
conjugate pairs of scalars as

\begin{split}&\tilde{\mathsf{G}}^{\star}_{(m,n)\mu_{1}\cdots\mu_{m}}(p_{1},\dots,p_{m};q_{1},\ldots,q_{n};\bar{q}_{1},\ldots,\bar{q}_{n})\\[4.0pt]
&\hskip 56.9055pt:=\mathsf{P}^{\prime}_{\hbar,\mathrm{int}}\big(\mathtt{v}_{\mu_{1}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{1}}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{v}_{\mu_{m}}\,\mathtt{e}^{p_{m}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{q_{1}}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{e}^{q_{n}}\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{\bar{q}_{1}}\odot_{\star}\cdots\odot_{\star}\mathtt{\bar{e}}^{\bar{q}_{n}}\big)\ .\end{split}

(5.66)

Then the general Ward-Takahashi identity (
5.41
) reads as

\small\begin{split}&p_{1\,\mu_{1}}\,D^{\star\mu_{1}}_{(m,n)\mu_{2}\cdots\mu_{m}}(p_{1},\ldots,p_{m};q_{1},\ldots,q_{n};\bar{q}_{1},\ldots,\bar{q}_{n})\\[4.0pt]
&=-\mathrm{i}\,\hbar\,g\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\mathrm{i}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2\cdots m}}\,\bigg(\sum_{j=1}^{n}\,\mathrm{e}^{\,\mathrm{i}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,(q_{1\cdots(j-1)}+\frac{1}{2}\,q_{j})}\\
&\hskip 142.26378pt\times\tilde{\mathsf{G}}^{\star}_{(m-1,n)\mu_{2}\cdots\mu_{m}}(p_{2},\ldots,p_{m};q_{1},\ldots,q_{j}-p_{1},\ldots,q_{n};\bar{q}_{1},\ldots,\bar{q}_{n})\\
&\hskip 99.58464pt-\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,q_{1\cdots n}}\,\sum_{j=1}^{n}\,\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,(\bar{q}_{1\cdots(j-1)}+\frac{1}{2}\,\bar{q}_{j})}\\
&\hskip 142.26378pt\times\tilde{\mathsf{G}}^{\star}_{(m-1,n)\mu_{2}\cdots\mu_{m}}(p_{2},\ldots,p_{m};q_{1},\ldots,q_{n};\bar{q}_{1},\ldots,\bar{q}_{j}-p_{1},\ldots,\bar{q}_{n})\bigg)\ .\end{split}\normalsize

(5.67)

Graphically, the general form of the non-anomalous Ward-Takahashi identity (
5.67
) is

(5.68)

In this diagram we denoted with a bullet point on the external photon leg labelled by
(\mu_{1},p_{1})
the amputation by the free photon propagator.
The half-phases appearing on the right-hand side in these formulas are results of the operator
\{\mathtt{\tilde{e}}_{p_{1}},-\}_{\star}\,Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}
acting on the scalar legs and their conjugates.
The overall phase
\mathrm{e}^{\,\mathrm{i}\,p_{1}\cdot\theta\,p_{2\cdots m}}
stems from
Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}
acting trivially on photon antifields, so the operator
\{\mathtt{\tilde{e}}_{p_{1}},-\}_{\star}\,Q^{\textrm{\tiny(3)}}_{\textrm{\tiny BRST}}
simply jumps over the photon legs.
The full phases are the braiding due to this operator moving past each leg in succession.
